subject: Arabic
framework: National Curriculum in England (2013): Languages programmes of study, key stage 2 (foreign language) and key stage 3 (modern foreign language)
statusNote: The gov.uk statutory guidance page for the languages programmes of study was opened and summarised; the two programme-of-study PDFs were not separately opened. Arabic is not named in the programmes, but KS2 allows any modern or ancient foreign language and KS3 any modern foreign language. Status Provisional. November 2026 alignment with the school's own Arabic files: Years 7 to 9 follow the Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work (topic per half term) and the Arabic Curriculum Intent (grammar points, assessments); Years 3 to 6 keep Kitabi (pupils placed by level) with the half-term topics and grammar focus of the Tarbiyyah Primary Year 3 to 6 curriculum maps (2023-24). The founding year teaches Spring 1 to Summer 2 from Mon 11 Jan 2027, after induction week (4 to 8 Jan, no live lessons); Spring 1 weeks 1 and 2 (11 and 18 Jan) are a bridge of the Autumn essentials.

GOV.UK: National curriculum in England: languages programmes of study (publication page)
Pearson GCSE (9-1) Arabic 1AA0 specification, Issue 5 (for KS4 themes)

purpose: To give pupils an opening to other languages and cultures.
To help pupils understand and respond to spoken and written language and to communicate for practical purposes.
To speak with growing confidence, write accurately and appreciate the language's writing.

keyStages.years: Years 3 to 6 (Reception to Year 2 optional, not statutory)

statements: Listen attentively and respond; use songs and rhymes to link sound, spelling and meaning.
Ask and answer questions, give opinions, speak in sentences and use accurate pronunciation.
Read carefully and build vocabulary; enjoy stories, songs, poems and rhymes.
Write phrases from memory and adapt them to describe people, places, things and actions.
Understand basic grammar of the language, including gender forms, key verbs and comparison with English.
Use present, past and future tenses; key structures; a wide vocabulary for opinions; accurate spelling.
Listen for information, start and develop conversations and speak with clear pronunciation.
Read original and adapted texts, translate short passages and read literary texts.
Write prose and creative texts, including short translations into the language.

toKS4: The KS3 scheme feeds the Pearson GCSE Arabic (1AA0) themes in the order the school's GCSE scheme of work teaches them. Y8 About me, My family and Hobbies and Y9 What does he look like? feed Theme 1 Who am I? (1.1) and Cultural life (1.3); Y8 At home and Y9 Food feed Daily life (1.2); Y9 My town and Transport feed Theme 2 Town, region and country (2.3) and Travel (2.2); Y9 Clothes feeds shopping (1.2, 2.2); Y9 At school feeds Theme 3 (3.1); Y8 My job feeds Theme 4 Work (4.3). Y9 Summer 2 ends with an introduction to the GCSE course. The same grammar (agreement, plurals, tenses, imperative, participles) serves 4AA1 Paper 1 grammar.

links.topic: Vocabulary of worship, belief and manners
links.how: Arabic terms such as salah, wudu and iman are used in both subjects; Arabic gives the language, Islamic Studies the meaning.
Qur'an lessons secure script and sounds; Arabic lessons add words, grammar and communication.
Words that pupils meet in recitation can be recognised in Arabic lessons.

links.topic: Grammar terminology (gender, plural, tense) and comparison with English
links.how: English grammar vocabulary helps pupils compare Arabic with English, as the KS2 programme expects.
KS3 expects short translation; English supports precision of meaning and expression.
Maths number work supports counting and shopping vocabulary; the word 'algebra' comes from al-Khwarizmi's al-jabr, a modest, accurate link.
Geography gives places and climates described in Arabic and in 1AA0 Theme 2.
Context for culture topics in the programme and 1AA0 Theme 1 Cultural life.
PSHE issues supply opinions that pupils can express in simple Arabic.

links.topic: Typing and reading Arabic script on devices
links.how: Using Arabic keyboards supports writing and awareness of right-to-left text.

gaps: The KS2 and KS3 programme-of-study PDFs were not opened separately; wording is paraphrased from the gov.uk statutory guidance page.
The KS3 programme does not give separate listening, speaking, reading and writing headings; here they appear under linguistic competence.
Years 1 and 2: the Tarbiyyah Primary maps show Arabic letters, numbers, colours and seasons; TGA teaches no separate Arabic in Years 1 and 2 (Qaidah sits in Qur'an), so they are not mapped here.
Years 3 to 6 topics are from the school's 2023-24 primary maps; TO CONFIRM: the Kitabi book and unit for each topic, and how online placement by level is done.
Primary map topics adapted to house rules: Mother's Day taught as kindness to parents (Y4), the birthday topic as dates only (Y5), a school trip and a school party as reading dialogues only (Y6).
Portal Arabic lessons were written for the earlier plan: y7 lessons 7 and 8 now fit Year 8, y8 lessons 9 to 12 fit Year 9 Autumn 2; most new units need new lessons.
No vocabulary or grammar list for KS3 is prescribed by the National Curriculum; the lists here follow the school's scheme and intent.
School choice: where the programme of study mentions songs, lessons use chants, rhymes and call-and-response without music.
